offence_severity: imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than seven years but which may extend to imprisonment for life
number_of_offences: Charged under Sections 304B, 498A IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act; finally upheld under Sections 304B and 498A IPC
key_evidence_accepted: Prosecution established beyond reasonable doubt that soon before death the deceased was subjected to cruelty and harassment by her husband and in-laws in connection with demand of dowry.
witness_credibility: Evidence of PW-1 regarding making payments to the appellants is cogent and consistent and is amply strengthened by the bank statements. Non-mention of details of money paid to the appellants and the demand of dowry and cruelty and harassment meted out to the deceased in the statement of PW-1 does not affect the credibility of PW-1. By perusal of evidence of brother of the deceased (PW-2), it is seen that he remained consistent throughout his cross-examination and nothing substantial was elicited to discredit his version.
trial_duration: Dates of offence: 13.08.1997; Trial judgment: 04.02.2002; High Court decision: 26.09.2011; Supreme Court decision: 28.07.2015
legal_representation: K. T. S. Tulsi, Siddharth Luthra, M. A. Chinnasamy, V. Senthil Kumar, Satyawan Rathi for the Appellants; R. K. Das, Mukesh Giri, AAG, Dinesh Kumar Garg, Deepak Mishra, Bhim Pratap Singh, Dr. Abhishek Atrey, Sumitra Rajora, Raj Kamal for the Respondents
investigation_status: FIR registered, charge sheet filed, trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: conviction and sentence confirmed; High Court: conviction and sentence confirmed; Supreme Court: partly allowed, conviction upheld, sentences reduced
prosecution_argument: Prosecution established beyond reasonable doubt that soon before death the deceased was subjected to cruelty and harassment by her husband and in-laws in connection with demand of dowry.
defence_argument: Accused contended that the FIR did not mention dowry demand or harassment, PW-2's statement was false and the investigation was flawed, and the suicide note and inland letter were fabricated.
legal_principle_applied: Conjoint reading of Section 1138 of the Evidence Act and Section 3048 IPC shows that there must be material to show that soon before her death the victim was subjected to cruelty or harassment.
precedent_relied_upon: Sunil Kumar & Anr. vs. State of Rajasthan (2005) 9 SCC 283; Sher Singh @ Partapa vs. State of Haryana (2015) 1 SCR 29; Ramakant Mishra @ Lalu etc. vs. State of U.P 2015 (3) SCALE 186; Kuwant Singh & Ors. vs. State of Punjab (2013) 4 SCC 177
sentencing_rationale: For the offence under Section 3048 IPC, the punishment is imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than seven years but which may extend to imprisonment for life. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and the occurrence was of the year 1997, interest of justice would be met if life imprisonment awarded to Rahul Mishra is reduced to imprisonment for a period of ten years and life imprisonment imposed on V.K. Mishra and Neelima Mishra is also reduced to imprisonment of seven years each.
judicial_mitigating_factors: Age and ailments of the accused, their imprisonment duration, and the occurrence was of the year 1997.
